title: Repair accepted DATA PING producer and handoff lineage gap
objective: Diagnose why current handoff reports latest_accepted_data_ping as unavailable while the accepted DATA PING bridge implementation remains on current main and its expected accepted-root is absent. Implement the smallest code-only repair that restores truthful producer/activation/lineage semantics without fabricating or backfilling accepted packets and without substituting Action Compass receipts for accepted packets unless an existing authoritative owner explicitly requires that mapping.

secondary_targets: tests directly covering accepted DATA PING bridge and latest handoff behavior
an exact existing accepted-DATA-PING producer or activation workflow only if fresh-state repository discovery proves that workflow is the current owner

evidence.summary: Current handoff exposes latest_accepted_data_ping as unavailable/null.
The path consumed by build_latest_handoff.py is absent on current main rather than containing immutable accepted packets.
Current main retains an implementation intended to canonicalize, hash, deduplicate and persist immutable accepted DATA PING packets and sidecar receipts.
The current handoff builder still scans research/data_ping_bridge/accepted and therefore treats this lineage as an active routing surface.

reproduction: Read current main LATEST_HANDOFF.json and observe latest_accepted_data_ping is null/unavailable.
Read scripts/architecture/build_latest_handoff.py and confirm the pointer is built from research/data_ping_bridge/accepted.
Attempt to enumerate research/data_ping_bridge/accepted on current main and confirm the expected root is absent.
Read scripts/data_ping/accepted_data_ping_bridge.py and confirm the accepted-packet persistence implementation still exists.
Determine from current repository wiring whether the defect is a missing producer/activation path, a retired-but-not-declared surface, or another bounded lineage defect before changing code.

positive: A fresh-state test demonstrates truthful accepted-packet lineage: when an immutable accepted packet exists, latest handoff resolves to that exact packet path and hash; when none exists, handoff explicitly remains unavailable without implying a fabricated packet.
Accepted DATA PING bridge preserves deterministic snapshot deduplication so replaying the same snapshot does not create a second accepted packet.
Tests cover missing accepted-root, present accepted-root and duplicate-snapshot behavior.
If a producer/activation path is repaired, one production-shape run or equivalent repository-integrated test proves the writer and handoff consumer agree on path and contract.

If current architecture intentionally retired the accepted bridge, the repair makes that retirement explicit in the existing routing surface rather than silently redirecting to an unrelated receipt class.
negative: Do not fabricate, reconstruct or backfill historical accepted DATA PING packets.
Do not map Action Compass receipts to accepted DATA PING packets without pre-existing authoritative repository ownership for that mapping.
Do not alter market gates, thresholds, model weights, portfolio logic, canonical market state, Action Compass decision semantics or API budget.
Do not add a new parallel accepted-ping engine or pointer when the existing owner can be repaired.

post_fix_gate: CI must pass, main readback must prove truthful accepted-ping pointer semantics, and a production-shape observation must not create duplicate or fabricated accepted packets.
